evals.prompt: Use $rrm-blog-copywriter to draft a blog post from the canonical brand guide, approved aviation fact-check context, and the raw topic 'how long does flight school take'.
evals.expected_output: A complete blog draft with SEO metadata, direct opening answer, useful decision sections, FAQ, CTA, section-level internal links, financing mention, useful bold emphasis, and only approved claims.
expectations: Uses the brand guide as the source of durable strategy
Owns per-post SEO title, slug, meta description, angle, outline, links, and CTA planning
Does not invent aviation or client claims
Explains timeline tradeoffs clearly
Includes FAQ and CTA
Mentions financing at least once with supported or qualified wording
Plans at least one internal backlink for every section
Stays in blog-post format

evals.prompt: Write a landing page for a flight school's instrument rating program using $rrm-blog-copywriter.
evals.expected_output: A refusal or redirect explaining that the skill is blog-only and should not write landing pages.
expectations: Does not produce landing page copy
Explains the skill boundary
Suggests using or creating a separate copywriting skill

evals.prompt: Improve an existing blog post draft with weak evidence and no fact-check report.
evals.expected_output: A response that identifies missing strategic or fact-checking inputs before rewriting unsupported claims.
expectations: Does not pad weak evidence
Requests missing brand guide or fact-check inputs
Can still suggest structural improvements
Keeps unsupported aviation claims out of the final draft

evals.prompt: Use $rrm-blog-copywriter to create a new blog post file in an Astro repo where src/content/config.ts defines required blog fields: title, description, author, authorImage, tags, categories, readingTime, pubDate, and updDate.
evals.expected_output: A schema-valid .md blog post file in the resolved blog content folder with frontmatter that matches the live blog collection schema and existing repo conventions, including a non-reused heroImage when that field is present.
expectations: Inspects the live content config before writing
Creates exactly one .md file by default
Includes all required blog frontmatter fields
Uses a .md filename that is the normalized-title slug
Uses only allowed category values
Reports the created file path and schema assumptions
Checks that heroImage is not reused from another existing blog post when present

evals.prompt: Create a repo-ready blog file from the brand guide and approved aviation facts in an Astro project that already has blog posts and a schema helper.
evals.expected_output: A repo-compatible blog post that matches existing frontmatter conventions, does not reuse an existing heroImage, and does not duplicate structured data if the repo already handles it.
expectations: Inspects existing posts before choosing frontmatter format
Matches date, image, tag, and category conventions
Uses at least 3 body image figures with figcaptions ending in (Source: {COMPANY_NAME} media archive)
Chooses a heroImage that has not already been used by another blog post when heroImage is present
Uses only public-subfolder paths for body figure images and verifies the files exist with the validator script
Does not hardcode a generic schema
Does not duplicate existing structured-data helpers

evals.prompt: Use $rrm-blog-copywriter to create a repo-ready Astro blog post with three body figure images in a repo that stores optimized body images under public/blog and frontmatter images under src/assets.
evals.expected_output: A schema-valid .md blog post with at least three body <figure> image blocks whose src values point to existing public subfolder files such as /blog/example.jpg, whose figcaptions end with (Source: {COMPANY_NAME} media archive), whose heroImage is not reused when present, and whose frontmatter image fields continue to follow the repo schema conventions.
expectations: Distinguishes frontmatter image conventions from Markdown body image rendering
Uses raw HTML
Does not use /src/assets, src/assets, or ../assets paths inside body figures
Verifies each body figure src resolves to a file under a public subfolder by running the body image validator script
Uses the validator script to catch heroImage reuse when heroImage is present
Ensures every figcaption ends with the exact media archive source suffix
Includes descriptive alt text for each body figure image

evals.prompt: Use $rrm-blog-copywriter to plan a post from the raw title 'instrument rating cost'.
evals.expected_output: A blog plan with an SEO title that places the keyword near the front, uses the current year because cost content is time-sensitive, stays within the title length guardrails, includes a valid slug, and includes a 120-160 character meta description when possible.
expectations: Does not copy the raw title unchanged
Uses a current-year title for cost intent
Makes the SEO title benefit-led and click-worthy without clickbait
Keeps the SEO title at 50-60 characters when possible and not over 65
Generates a lowercase kebab-case filename/slug from the full final title, not a shortened fragment
Includes CTA, section-level internal links, financing mention, program page link opportunities, and claims needing fact-check

evals.prompt: Use $rrm-blog-copywriter to plan a post from the raw title 'what is a cfii'.
evals.expected_output: A blog plan with a question-format SEO title because the search intent is question-based, plus a readable slug, meta description, angle, and aviation claims to verify.
expectations: Uses question format for question-based intent
Explains CFII in plain language
Makes the SEO title promise a clear answer without unsupported hype
Does not add the current year unless freshness is justified
Keeps the title within SEO length guardrails
Lists aviation claims needing fact-check

evals.prompt: Use $rrm-blog-copywriter to plan a post from the raw title 'part 141 flight schools in [target state]'.
evals.expected_output: A blog plan with an SEO title that uses the primary keyword or close variant near the front, handles the target location naturally, uses the current year only if framed as a comparison or guide, and avoids question format unless the search intent requires it.
expectations: Does not default to a question title for non-question intent
Uses the target location and Part 141 terminology naturally
Makes the SEO title useful to the searcher without clickbait
Uses the current year only if the plan frames the post as a freshness-sensitive guide or comparison
Keeps the title within SEO length guardrails
Generates a lowercase kebab-case filename/slug from the full final title, not a shortened fragment

evals.prompt: Use $rrm-blog-copywriter to create a blog post from the brand guide and latest fact-check report. The user does not repeat the topic in this prompt.
evals.expected_output: A blog plan and post that use the fact-check report Topic Context as the raw topic/title source before creating the SEO title, normalized-title filename/slug, meta description, angle, outline, links, and CTA.
expectations: Reads Topic Context from the fact-check report
Does not ask the user to repeat the same raw topic/title
Uses the Topic Context to create the SEO title and normalized-title filename/slug
Uses approved language, avoid list, and qualifiers from the same fact-check report

evals.prompt: Use $rrm-blog-copywriter to improve a mechanically correct flight school blog draft that has generic H2s, repeated phrases like 'that matters' and 'in plain English', excessive source-report wording, and a final CTA with several competing links.
evals.expected_output: A revised blog post that keeps verified claims, rewrites the opening with reader stakes or a concrete aviation moment, replaces label headings with editorial promises, removes robotic phrase repetition, places qualifiers once near the claims they limit, and ends with one primary CTA.
expectations: Keeps aviation claims within the fact-check report
Adds human hook, reader stakes, company POV, and sourced scene/example to planning
Rewrites generic H2s into reader-value promises
Removes repeated robotic transitions and source-report texture
Avoids over-hedging verified claims
Ends with one primary CTA
Runs the human voice lint script before delivery

evals.prompt: Use $rrm-blog-copywriter to create a new blog post from a strong brand guide and approved aviation fact-check report.
evals.expected_output: A schema-valid blog post that passes the image/link validator and human voice lint script, with a direct but human opening, specific aviation scenarios, editorial headings, precise qualifiers, FAQ friction answers, and one CTA.
expectations: Plans a human hook before drafting
Makes aviation feel serious, exciting, and attainable without unsupported hype
Turns client proof into scenarios, mechanisms, or consequences
Uses qualified safety, cost, timeline, and career language without blanket disclaimers
Avoids label headings and generic SEO texture
Runs validate-blog-body-images with --fix and without --fix
Runs lint-blog-human-voice and revises until it passes

evals.prompt: Use $rrm-blog-copywriter to revise a flight school blog draft that says 'The current fleet page shows...', 'listed in the repo as FAA-approved', 'the exact current aircraft count should be confirmed', and 'Ask the school how its flight simulator is used'.
evals.expected_output: A revised blog post that removes outside-reviewer and source-audit voice, translates supported facts into company-seat language, omits or generalizes unverified exact details, and passes the human voice lint script.
expectations: Rewrites company-specific facts with we, our, or us after the first company reference
Removes repo, current-page, episode-notes, and source-audit phrasing from final copy
Does not tell the reader to ask the named client what the client does
Handles uncertain current details by omission, supported generalization, or one natural contact-us sentence
Keeps you/your language more frequent than we/our/us
Runs lint-blog-human-voice and revises until it passes

evals.prompt: Use $rrm-blog-copywriter to create a blog post with authorContext: 'Author: School Name Team'.
evals.expected_output: A schema-valid blog post credited to the team that sounds like warm school staff speaking to prospective students, not like an outside evaluator or agency summary.
expectations: Uses the team byline in frontmatter when it matches the live schema
Writes from the school's seat with we/our/us for company-specific facts
Keeps you/your language more frequent than company pronouns
Does not add fake personal anecdotes or named-author persona
Avoids page-summary, repo, source-audit, and ask-the-school phrasing
Runs lint-blog-human-voice and revises until it passes

evals.prompt: Use $rrm-blog-copywriter to create a blog post with authorContext: 'Author: Alex Rivera. Source-backed background: former military pilot and current chief flight instructor.'
evals.expected_output: A schema-valid blog post credited to Alex Rivera that uses light, relevant, source-backed military or instructor voice cues without turning the article into a first-person memoir.
expectations: Uses the named author in frontmatter when it matches the live schema
Uses military or instructor language only when useful to the topic
Does not invent service history, credentials, missions, aircraft, or personal anecdotes
Avoids first-person singular unless existing authored posts or prompt notes clearly support it
Keeps the article primarily reader-focused and school-staff warm
Runs lint-blog-human-voice and revises until it passes

evals.prompt: Use $rrm-blog-copywriter to create a blog post with authorContext: 'Author: Jamie Lee' and no available author bio or background source.
evals.expected_output: A schema-valid blog post that keeps Jamie Lee as the credited author but falls back to the school's team voice instead of inventing a persona.
expectations: Keeps the named author credit when the schema requires author frontmatter
Uses team voice in the body because no usable author background exists
Does not invent credentials, aviation history, airline experience, or personal stories
Writes from inside the school rather than as an outside evaluator
Runs lint-blog-human-voice and revises until it passes

evals.prompt: Use $rrm-blog-copywriter to revise a flight school blog draft that says 'Our rentals page lists aircraft available for checkout' and 'Our website says students can rent after approval'.
evals.expected_output: A revised blog post that removes page-as-source phrasing and rewrites supported facts into direct, warm company language such as 'Here at the school, our rental options include...' or 'We can help you confirm current rental availability.'
expectations: Rewrites our-page and website-source phrasing into direct company offer language
Does not publish page lists, page shows, website says, or source-audit wording
Uses a natural contact-us sentence only when a current detail genuinely needs confirmation
Keeps verified rental facts confident and warm
Runs lint-blog-human-voice and revises until it passes
